meta.seo_title: Engineering Company Google Ads Case Study | PPC Guru
meta.meta_description: How PPC Guru launched a Toronto engineering firm on Google Ads, delivering 12 genuine call and quote-request leads in its first full month with tracking built in from day one.

headline: Launching an Engineering Firm to 12 Google Ads Leads in Month One
summary_line: PPC Guru launched Vin Engineering on Google Ads with call and quote-form tracking in place, and the firm's first full month (July 2026) delivered 12 genuine leads — eight online quote requests and four phone calls — from a single focused permit-offer Search campaign.
client_context: Vin Engineering INC is an engineering-services firm based in Toronto, Ontario, Canada, offering city-permit and engineering-drawing services to homeowners and contractors. Its enquiries are considered, higher-value requests — a call or a quote form from someone who needs stamped drawings or permit support for a project. Google Ads reaches those searchers at the point of need, so capturing each call and quote request accurately is central to the account from the very first month.
background: Vin Engineering partnered with PPC Guru in mid-2026 to launch its Google Ads presence. As a fresh build, the plan was a single, tightly focused Search campaign around a clear city-permit offer, paired with call and lead-form tracking so every genuine enquiry could be measured from day one.
analysis: PPC Guru built the account around one focused Search campaign tied to a specific permit offer, and set up conversion tracking first: website and ad call tracking, plus lead-form conversions for the site's main and pop-up quote forms. With a clear offer and clean tracking, early budget could be judged on genuine enquiries rather than clicks.
analysis_points: Launch a single, focused Search campaign around a clear city-permit offer.
Set up call tracking for both website calls and ad calls to the Toronto line.
Add lead-form conversions for the main and pop-up quote forms.
Judge early spend on genuine calls and quote requests, not clicks.

timeline.what: PPC Guru launch — permit-offer Search campaign live with call and form tracking; a short ramp month as the campaign entered learning.
First full month delivered 12 genuine leads — eight online quote requests and four phone calls.

challenge: As a brand-new account with a specialized, higher-value service, Vin Engineering had to build genuine demand from a standing start, with no history for bidding to learn from and lower monthly enquiry volumes than a high-frequency consumer service. That makes clean tracking of every call and quote request essential, so early budget decisions rest on real enquiries rather than raw clicks.

changes.why: Concentrated budget on a clear city-permit offer instead of spreading it thin.
Captured phone enquiries to the Toronto line as measurable conversions.
Tracked both the main and pop-up lead forms so quote requests counted as leads.
Pointed bidding at genuine calls and quote requests as early data accumulated.

technical.label: Lead signals
technical.value: Website calls · Ad calls · Quote forms

benchmark: June 2026 was a short launch-ramp month while the campaign entered learning, so it is shown for context, not as a like-for-like comparison. The headline is the first full month (July 2026): 12 genuine leads at about $124 each — reasonable for a specialized, higher-value engineering service. This is a very early snapshot on a young account.
gradual: The account moved from a brief launch ramp in June 2026 — when the campaign was still entering Google's learning phase — to a first full month in July 2026 that produced 12 genuine leads, split between eight online quote requests and four phone calls. It is an encouraging opening month, but a single full month is not yet a trend; the picture should be re-confirmed once the account completes a full quarter.
lessons: Track calls and quote requests from day one — for higher-value services, every enquiry counts.
Anchor a new campaign to one clear offer so budget and messaging stay focused.
Expect a short learning ramp before a new account's first full month of volume.
Judge early spend on genuine enquiries, not clicks.
Give a specialized, lower-volume account a full quarter before drawing conclusions.
why_it_worked: Call and quote-form tracking was in place from the first day of spend.
A single focused Search campaign kept budget on a clear permit offer.
Both online quote requests and phone calls were captured as genuine leads.
The first full month produced measurable enquiries, not just clicks.
outcome: Vin Engineering has an early but working Google Ads lead engine: after a short launch ramp in June 2026, its first full month (July 2026) delivered 12 genuine leads — eight online quote requests and four phone calls — at about $124 each from a single focused permit-offer campaign. This is a very early snapshot on a young account. PPC Guru's recommended next step is to let the account complete a full quarter and re-confirm the trend before scaling budget.
cta: PPC Guru helps Canadian professional-services and engineering firms turn search demand into tracked calls and quote requests with focused Google Ads.
methodology: All figures are pulled directly from the client's Google Ads account and shown on a monthly basis. 'Genuine leads' are phone calls and quote-form submissions only. The account has only two months of history (Jun–Jul 2026); June is a partial launch-ramp month, so July 2026 is treated as the first full month.
lead_quality: Genuine leads are a mix of online quote requests and direct phone calls to the firm's Toronto line — considered, higher-value enquiries typical of engineering and permit services.
teaser: 📐 Engineering Google Ads launch: PPC Guru started Vin Engineering on a focused permit-offer campaign and delivered 12 genuine leads (8 quote requests + 4 calls) in its first full month (Jul 2026) — tracking built in from day one.
